climate.title: Your field's climate fingerprint
climate.body: Each season in a few numbers, with the hardest ones picked out.
climate.loading: Reading your field's weather and soil moisture record…
climate.empty.title: Not enough weather data yet
climate.empty.body: The fingerprint needs at least one full season of daily weather. It appears once the field's data loads.
climate.pick.title: Season by season
climate.pick.body: Pick a season to read its numbers. Orange stripes were drier, blue were wetter.
climate.pick.label: Seasons of your field
climate.pick.caption: Season {season}: {rain} mm of rain
climate.cards.title: Season {season}
climate.ind.rain.title: Rainfall
climate.ind.rain.explain: Total rain that fell in the season; below the typical season means a dry year.
climate.ind.heavyRain.title: Heaviest rain in one day
climate.ind.heavyRain.explain: The most rain in a single day, which drives runoff and soil erosion.
climate.ind.drySpell.title: Longest dry spell
climate.ind.drySpell.explain: The longest run of days with less than 1 mm of rain, when crops can run short of water.
climate.ind.frost.title: Frost days
climate.ind.frost.explain: Days when the night fell below 0 °C, which can damage young or flowering crops.
climate.ind.hardFrost.title: Hard frost days
climate.ind.hardFrost.explain: Days when the night fell below -2 °C, cold enough to harm most crops.
climate.ind.hot.title: Hot days
climate.ind.hot.explain: Days warmer than 30 °C, when many crops lose water faster.
climate.ind.veryHot.title: Very hot days
climate.ind.veryHot.explain: Days warmer than 35 °C, which can hurt flowering and grain filling.
climate.ind.gdd.title: Warmth for growth
climate.ind.gdd.explain: Growing degree-days above 5 °C: the heat available for crops to grow and ripen.
climate.ind.et0.title: Water the air could take
climate.ind.et0.explain: Reference evapotranspiration: how much water a well-watered grass field would use.
climate.ind.balance.title: Rain minus water demand
climate.ind.balance.explain: Rainfall minus the water the air could take; strongly negative means the season ran dry.
climate.ind.soil.title: Soil moisture compared with other seasons
climate.ind.soil.explain: How much wetter or drier the root zone was than in the other seasons; below zero is drier.
climate.stripes.title: Climate stripes
climate.stripes.body: One stripe per season. Hover or focus a stripe for its numbers.
climate.stripes.warmth.caption: Season {season}: {gdd} degree-days of warmth
climate.stripes.dryness.caption: Season {season}: rain minus water demand {balance} mm
climate.calendar.title: Anomaly calendar
climate.calendar.body: Each square is a month against the same month in other seasons. Blue was wetter, orange drier.
climate.calendar.rain: Rain compared with the same month in other seasons, percent
climate.calendar.soil: Soil moisture compared with the same month in other seasons
climate.calendar.table: Show the numbers as a table
climate.worst.title: Hardest seasons on record
climate.worst.body: The three worst seasons for each kind of trouble. Replay one to see how each rotation would have coped.
climate.worst.none: No season in this record had this problem.
climate.worst.sentence.rain: {season}: only {rain} mm of rain, {pct}% below the average season.
climate.worst.sentence.soil: {season}: soil moisture was {z} standard deviations below the other seasons.
